### Homework instructions

#### Make a map **using Quarto** with one of the following TidyTuesday datasets. Save your script and output appropriately.

Load libraries

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
```

Load data. I will use the cat dataset from TidyTuesday, so I will just copy and paste / follow the instructions for loading the data from online.

```{r}
# Get the Data

# Read in with tidytuesdayR package 
# Install from CRAN via: 
# install.packages("tidytuesdayR")
# This loads the readme and all the datasets for the week of interest

# Either ISO-8601 date or year/week works!

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2023-01-31')
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2023, week = 5)

cats_uk <- tuesdata$cats_uk
cats_uk_reference <- tuesdata$cats_uk_reference
```

Get the UK data to link the cat data with

```{r}
# Was having a hard time getting UK from map_data("UK"), but after some investigation, it looks like I need to specify the database "world" first and then look for UK as the region (country). 
UK <- map_data("world", region = "UK")
head(UK)
```

Map just the UK

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "#012169",# UK royal blue
               color = "black") + # outlines
  theme_minimal() + #minimal theme
  guides(fill = "none") + # no legend
  labs(x = "Longitude (deg)", y = "Latitude (deg)") +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "white"))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator") # formatting of shape looks better
```

I want to plot only one cat and their positions, so first I will figure out which cat has the most position data points.

```{r}
#count(cats_uk$tag_id) <- this did not work

cats_uk |> 
  count(tag_id, sort = TRUE) # sort made it easier to see high to low.
```

Choosing "Tom" instead because I like his name.

```{r}
Tom <- cats_uk |> 
  filter(tag_id == "Tom-Tag")
```

Place Tom's data on the map

```{r}
Tom_Map_UK_Whole <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "#012169",# UK royal blue
               color = "black") + # outlines
  geom_point(data = Tom,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat),
             color = "#C8102E",
             size = 4,
             alpha = 0.65) +
  theme_minimal() + #minimal theme
  guides(fill = "none") + # no legend
  labs(x = "Longitude (deg)", y = "Latitude (deg)") +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "white"))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator") # formatting of shape looks better

Tom_Map_UK_Whole
```

Try to zoom in on that area

```{r}
Tom_Turf <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "#012169",# UK royal blue
               color = "black") + # outlines
  geom_point(data = Tom,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat),
             color = "#C8102E",
             size = 4,
             alpha = 0.65) +
  theme_minimal() + #minimal theme
  guides(fill = "none") + # no legend
  labs(x = "Longitude (deg)", y = "Latitude (deg)") +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "white"))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator",
            xlim = c(-4.61, -4.59),
            ylim = c(50.43, 50.443))
  
Tom_Turf
```

Need to include regions within UK

```{r}
UK_cities <- world.cities |>
  filter(country.etc == "UK") # This world cities function seems like a good way to get the cities for most countries. I tried using the county method from class, but struggled a bit
```

What does this map look like?

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "#012169",# UK royal blue
               color = "black") + # outlines
  geom_point(data = UK_cities,
             aes(x = long, y = lat),
             color = "#C8102E",
             size = 2) +
  theme_minimal() + #minimal theme
  guides(fill = "none") + # no legend
  labs(x = "Longitude (deg)", y = "Latitude (deg)") +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "white"))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator") # formatting of shape looks better

```

The cities are points... that's not going to work. I may have to give up for now and accept just having Tom's data on the whole map of the UK... I will save this here.

```{r}
Tom_Map_UK_Whole <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "#012169",# UK royal blue
               color = "black") + # outlines
  geom_point(data = Tom,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat),
             color = "#C8102E",
             size = 4,
             alpha = 0.65) +
  theme_minimal() + #minimal theme
  guides(fill = "none") + # no legend
  labs(x = "Longitude (deg)", y = "Latitude (deg)") +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "white"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA) 
  )+ #White background all around
  coord_map(projection = "mercator") # formatting of shape looks better

Tom_Map_UK_Whole

ggsave(here("Week_07", "Output", "Week_07_Homework_Plot.png"))
```
